correctness.rationale: At each p-power level the valuation of the LCM subtracts one precisely if there is a divisible term. For p^j<=k at least one exists, and for p^j>k there is at most one, so the higher levels cancel. This yields the claimed local periods and CRT product over L_k, without needing minimality. For odd p the local numerator is an odd sum of signs, never zero. At p=2 write k+1=2^e+r with 1<=r<=2^e; a full dyadic block contributes 2^e-1 in truncated valuation, leaving a fixed sign times S_e(r). Since odd positions have sign +1 and the sign at 2u is minus the lower-level sign at u, an even-length block averages to twice the signed lower-level block sum, and an odd-length block is the signed difference of successive lower-level block sums. The e=1,2 arrays and induction establish a single midpoint zero: in the odd-index recurrence the odd lower-level index has valuation one, while the even one has valuation at least two or vanishes; in the even-index recurrence the factor two raises the valuation by one. The endpoints contribute ±2^e and the k=1 quotient is identically one. This proves the stated all-window equivalence for total prime multiplicity; no sign assertion for the other windows or least-period claim is needed.
residual_risks: Bounded checks corroborate but do not replace the dyadic induction. The window is of length k+1; the numbers 2,5,11,... listed for the test describe k, not the window length.
